source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
Nameless, it is the beginning of Heaven and earth; named, it is the mother of the ten thousand things.
Therefore, constantly free from desire, one observes its mystery.
Constantly possessing desire, one observes its manifestations.
These two arise from the same source but have different names; together they are called mysterious.
Mystery upon mystery: the gate of all mysteries.
When everyone under Heaven knows beauty as beauty, ugliness already exists.
When everyone knows goodness as goodness, non-goodness already exists.

Therefore being and non-being give rise to each other; difficulty and ease complete each other; length and shortness compare with each other; high and low incline toward each other; tones and sounds harmonize with each other; before and after follow each other.
Therefore the sage dwells in the affairs of non-action.
He practices teaching without words; the ten thousand things arise, and he does not reject them; he brings them forth but does not possess them; he acts but does not rely on his achievement.
When the achievement is complete, he does not remain in it.
Precisely because he does not remain in it, it does not depart.

Do not esteem the worthy, and the people will not contend; do not value rare goods, and the people will not become thieves; do not display desirable things, and the people's hearts will not be disordered.
Therefore in the sage's governance, empty the people's hearts and fill their bellies.
Weaken their intentions and strengthen their bones.
Cause clever people not to dare to act.
Practice non-action, and nothing will remain ungoverned.

The Way is empty, yet its use may never be exhausted; deep indeed, it seems the ancestor of the ten thousand things. Blunt its sharpness, unravel its confusion, soften its brightness, and mingle with its dust; deep indeed, it seems perhaps to exist.
